guide.intro: Everything you need to run your first service, in order. Steps tick themselves off as you go.

screens.title: Connect your screens
screens.body: Open Outputs and set your projector or TV to Main output. Only have a laptop? Turn on Rehearsal / window mode to see the output in a small window.

output.title: Output
output.body: The monitor shows exactly what the room sees; Room / Next above it switches to the next slide (only on the monitor, never the screens). Under it, ◀ and ▶ step to the previous or next slide, with both shown small beside them: hover one to read it large, click it to show it. The strip beside it clears one layer at a time (messages, props, slide, media, background); the red power button turns everything off. Below: Scenes for the screens with Black (⇧B), Logo (⇧L) and Freeze (⇧F) on the same row, then the lower third. While a video plays behind the words, the speaker on the monitor turns its sound on or off.

controls.body: Under the monitor: the stage message, timers, messages with fill-in fields, and props. Anything you start here shows on the screens straight away.

media.title: Media bin
media.body: Open it with Media in the toolbar: pictures and videos you import, and the built-in still and motion backgrounds. Click to show, double-click to add to the playlist, or drag onto the slides.

live.title: Going live
live.help: Streaming and recording the service, from the first stream to the low-delay links.

youtube.a:
1. Click Live in the toolbar to open the Live console.
2. Under Destinations click Add and pick YouTube or Facebook.
3. Copy the stream key. In YouTube Studio: Go live › Stream, then the copy button beside “Stream key” (not the Stream URL). On Facebook: Live video › Streaming software.
4. Paste it into the destination and click Save key. Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again.
5. Click Go live. The dot beside the destination turns green once the service is receiving.
Any other service that gives you an RTMP address works as Custom RTMP: paste its server address, then its key.
If the internet drops while you’re live, Lampstand keeps the stream on and reconnects by itself for up to 10 minutes (the console says Reconnecting; a recording carries on). In YouTube Studio, turn off “Enable Auto-stop” in the stream’s settings, so YouTube keeps the broadcast open while it reconnects.

console.a:
1. Click Live in the toolbar to dock the console beside the output, or click the pop-out button to give it its own window (on another display, say).
2. Go live or Record with the two buttons at the top.
3. Watch the picture: it is exactly what goes out. The L/R meter on its left is the stream’s sound. It works before you go live too, so speak and check it moves.
4. Under the picture, click a scene to change what the stream shows. Scenes are in three tabs, each a row of small live previews (slide it sideways if there are more). Slides: Main screen, Words on black, Black. Cameras: the Switcher (it follows Cut, Auto and the T-bar), every camera, and with two cameras, Two cameras or Camera in a corner. Screens: the Alternate (HDMI) output or the Stage display. The one on air has a ring (red while streaming). The arrow beside Scenes folds them away. Under the scenes, “Lower third on the stream” puts the words along the bottom of whatever is on (the main screen, a camera, the switcher), or takes them off. Scene changes sets whether a change of scene or camera cuts or fades, and how fast.
5. Under the scenes, on one line: the speaker mutes the stream and the slider sets its level; then the mic. There is always one, the computer’s own to begin with. The mic button puts it on the stream (red) or takes it off, the box picks which mic it is (speak and watch the L/R meter on the picture), then its level and mute.
6. More mics or the desk, added in the Mixer, get a line each below.
7. Further down: the lower third’s look (while a scene with one is on air), music and video sound, destinations, quick settings and how the computer is coping.
If the stream goes out with no sound for a few seconds, a red notice under the picture says why (muted, no mic sent, or the mics are silent), with the fix. Hover any reading in the top and bottom bars to see what it means.

picture.q: Choose what the stream shows and hears
picture.a:
1. Click a scene under the stream picture (see “Use the Live console”): it sets what the stream shows, what’s behind the words, and the words.
2. With Two cameras or Camera in a corner on air, the two boxes under the scenes pick which camera goes where. Pick the other box’s camera to swap them.
3. With a lower third on air, “Lower third on the stream” further down sets its theme, its position (left, centre or right) and its size: Auto fits each slide, or turn Auto off and drag.
4. Mics and the desk are under the scenes; music and video are in “Music and video” further down: switch each one on for the stream and watch its meter.
For a look no scene gives (full-screen words over a camera, say), set the words and what’s behind them in Settings › Streaming.
Turn on “Show the stream picture before going live” to check it first.

record.a:
1. Click Record in the Live console. It records with or without streaming.
2. To record every time you go live, turn it on in Settings › Streaming.
The file stays playable even if the computer stops unexpectedly.

slow.q: Stream from an older or slower computer
slow.a:
1. Open Settings › Streaming › Performance.
2. Click “Check this computer” (a 10-second test) and leave the mode on Auto to use its answer.
3. Or choose yourself: Light (540p) for older laptops and slow internet, Balanced (720p) for most churches, Quality (1080p) for a recent computer with a good upload.
If the computer struggles mid-stream, the console offers Switch to Light: a two-second pause, and the stream carries on.
A slow upload is handled by itself: the stream lowers its bitrate to stay live (the bitrate reading turns amber) and climbs back when it can. If the upload stays too slow for the picture size, the console suggests Light, which looks sharper at that rate. Check your upload with any speed test: 1080p needs about 5 Mb/s, 720p 3, 540p 1.5.

delay.a:
1. Before going live, open YouTube Studio › Stream settings › Stream latency.
2. Pick Ultra low-latency (about 2–5 seconds; Low is 5–10, Normal 15–30).
3. Judge the delay on the public watch page: the preview inside YouTube Studio lags more.
Lampstand itself sends each frame about 0.2 seconds after it is drawn; the console’s delay reading shows this live. For under a second, use a direct link or NDI.

direct.q: Send to another room with almost no delay (direct link)
direct.a:
1. On the receiving computer, in OBS add a Media Source, untick “Local file”, and set Input to udp://@:9000. In VLC: Open Network, udp://@:9000, and lower “network caching”.
2. In the Live console, click Add › Direct link and type the receiver’s address with the same port, e.g. udp://192.168.1.50:9000.
3. Click Go live.
A direct link has well under a second of delay and can run beside YouTube. UDP is for the same network. Across the internet use SRT (srt://address:9000, with the receiver set to srt://:9000?mode=listener); it needs an ffmpeg built with SRT.

ndi.q: Send to vMix, OBS or NDI gear on the network
ndi.a:
1. Install NDI Tools (free) on this computer.
2. Open Settings › NDI and turn on a feed: the program, the words alone over transparency (to key over cameras), or the stream picture.
3. In vMix, OBS (with the NDI plugin) or NDI Studio Monitor, add an NDI source and pick this computer’s feed by name.
NDI stays on the local network and is the lowest-delay way to feed a video mixer.

screens.q: Show a lower third on the projector too
screens.a:
1. Under the output monitor, switch on “Lower third on the screens”.
2. Pick its theme and where it sits (left, centre or right).
The audience screens then draw every slide’s words along the bottom in that theme, over a camera or video, until you switch it off. The stream follows it unless the stream has a theme of its own.

keyFeed.q: Send the words to a video mixer over HDMI (key feed)
keyFeed.a:
1. Plug the video mixer into this computer’s HDMI output.
2. Open Outputs (the Audience light in the toolbar) and give that display the Alternate role.
3. Under “Alternate output: key feed for a video mixer”, pick Green or Blue (chroma key) or Black (luma key).
4. Click “Choose its themes”, pick Lower third, then click a theme and choose Alternate (HDMI) for Scripture, Lyrics and Text.
On an ATEM, use an upstream chroma or luma key with this input as the source. For a clean alpha channel instead, use the NDI “Words” feed.

trouble.q: Fix a stream that won’t start or keeps stopping
trouble.a:
1. Hover a destination that says Stopped to see why.
2. “Key needed”, or a key that doesn’t look right: copy the Stream key again (not the Stream URL) and save it.
3. Can’t connect: check the internet connection. Lampstand tries YouTube’s second address by itself.
4. Amber bitrate: the upload can’t carry the chosen quality and the stream has lowered itself to stay live. If it stays amber, pick a lighter Performance mode.
5. Picture jumps or readings turn red: the computer can’t keep up; pick a lighter mode.
Click Retry to bring a stopped destination back without ending the stream.

cover.q: Hide something from the stream for a moment
cover.a:
1. While streaming or recording, click Cover in the Live console.
2. Viewers (and the recording) see the cover picture instead; the sound carries on.
3. Click Uncover to show the service again.
Choose the cover picture in Settings › Streaming › Cover picture: the logo card, or one of your pictures or videos.

sendToStream.q: Put the slide on the stream while it shows a camera
sendToStream.a:
1. While streaming, if the stream shows something else (a camera, say), Send to stream appears on the live monitor.
2. Click it: the stream shows what the screens show, words and all.
3. Click On stream · Undo to put the stream back as it was.
Picking another scene meanwhile ends it, and that scene stays.

lowerThirdLayout.q: Place the stream’s lower third, and give the words more room
lowerThirdLayout.a:
1. In the Live console, with a lower-third scene on air, open Lower third on the stream.
2. Pick one of the six spots: top or bottom, left, centre or right.
3. Drag Width to let the words spread further across the picture: wider means fewer, longer lines, so a long verse isn’t squeezed into a narrow column.
The same settings are in Settings › Streaming.

howto.title: How to…
howto.help: Short step-by-step recipes for the everyday jobs. Click one to open it.

song.a:
1. Click + next to LIBRARY and choose New song (or press {{newSong}}).
2. Name it, pick its theme and, if you like, the playlist it goes in. Click Create.
3. It opens in Edit, expanded to the whole window, on its first slide and ready to type. Press ⇧⌘N (or Slide in the toolbar) for the next slide, or ⌥↩ to break a slide where the caret is. Double-click a slide to change its words; Esc stops typing.
4. Group in the toolbar (or right-click a slide in the list and choose Group) makes it the Chorus, Verse 2 and so on. Slides after it in the same group come too. Split breaks a slide that’s too long to fit.
5. It saves as you type. The Song tab on the right holds the title, authors, copyright, CCLI number and theme; the Text tab formats its words.
To paste a whole song at once, press Reflow: [Verse 1] and [Chorus] on their own lines start groups, and a blank line starts a slide.

playlist.a:
1. Click + next to PLAYLISTS to make a playlist.
2. Add sections (Walk-in, Worship, Word…) with the + above the items.
3. On the Show page, click the “+ Add to …” card at the end of a section (or the + on its coloured band) to add songs, verses, slides or media to it. You can also drag things onto the section.
4. Drag items to reorder them. A section moves with everything under it.
Deleting a section deletes everything in it. The … beside a playlist’s name renames, duplicates or deletes it; double-click the name to rename it too.

verse.q: Put a Bible verse on screen
verse.a:
1. Press {{quick}}.
2. Type a reference such as jn 3 16 or Romans 8:28-39.
3. Press Enter to load it on Preview, or Shift+Enter to put it straight on screen.
In the Bible workspace, clicking a verse opens it in the slides without touching the screen, so it never interrupts a presentation. Click the slide to show it, or double-click the verse to show it at once. Turn on “Click shows it now” there if you want a click to go straight on screen.

preview.q: Check slides before the room sees them
preview.a:
1. Turn on Preview first in the toolbar.
2. Click a slide: it loads on the Preview monitor only.
3. Press {{goLive}} (or Go live) to send it to the screens.

clear.a:
1. To clear one layer (text, media, background, overlays), use the strip beside the monitor.
2. To clear everything, click the red power button or press {{clearAll}}.
3. To clear the words but keep the background, press {{panic}}.
Black and Logo cover the screen without losing your place.

backgrounds.a:
1. Click the picture button in an item's header (or on its Background tile).
2. Hover a kind to see its backgrounds: Motion backgrounds, Built-in, Your backgrounds, or Your pictures and videos. Click one: it goes behind every slide of that item (and on screen at once if it's live).
3. A video behind the words starts silent. Tick “Play the video’s sound” in the same menu, or click the speaker on the live monitor, to hear it in the room and on the stream. It goes quiet while another video plays over it.
4. Busy picture? “Readability overlay” darkens it under the words: evenly, at the edges, or behind a band at the bottom or top, light, medium or strong.
Themes carry a background too; “The theme’s background” goes back to it. “Use this for all” gives every item in the service the same one.

arrangement.q: Change a song’s order, key or language
arrangement.a:
1. Open the song in Edit. The Song tab on the right holds its arrangements (a short version, say) and a translation.
2. On the Show page, pick the arrangement in the song’s header.
3. Transpose the chords there for the stage display, or turn on the translation to show it under each line.

tiles.q: Read the slide tiles, and jump to the chorus
tiles.a:
1. Each song, verse or set of slides starts with a Background tile: the picture behind all of its slides. Click it to put it on the screens behind the words; its button at the top left changes it.
2. The slides after it show only their words, over a checkerboard, because they sit on that background. A slide with a background of its own shows it.
3. To give one slide its own background, hover it and click the picture button at its top left. Pick “The same as the other slides” to undo it.
4. A letter at a slide's top left is its section's key: C for the Chorus, A, S, D for Verses 1–3, B for the Bridge, T for the Tag, P for the Pre-chorus. Press it to go to that section of the selected song (a chorus sung again goes to the next one).
5. Black, Logo, Freeze, play/pause and the switcher's Cut and Auto now take Shift: ⇧B, ⇧L, ⇧F, ⇧P, ⇧C, ⇧T.
6. A picture or video item shows two squares at its top left: the front one filled means it plays over everything, the back one filled means behind the words. Click to switch (if it's on screen, it moves at once).
7. At the bottom left, the orange button sets how slides change for everything (Cut, Fade, Dissolve…, or each theme's own) and the purple one how pictures and videos change (Cut or Dissolve, and how long). The shuffle button in an item's header gives just that item its own slide transition. Every song, verse and slide set has two more header buttons: the film strip moves its slides on by themselves (pick the seconds, and whether it loops back to the first), and the target plays it on the announcements layer (green while it's there).
8. At the bottom right: Grid, Easy (the words, large) or Table (a small picture, the words and the notes). “…” sets Slides by group (each section on its own row) and what shows through transparent thumbnails.

edit.q: Make your own slides, and find your way round the editor
edit.a:
1. Add Slides from the + menu. It opens in Edit, expanded to the whole window.
2. The toolbar along the top is the same for everything you edit. Text types the slide’s words and Slide adds a slide. Songs also have Group and Split; slides also have Text box, Rectangle, Ellipse, Line and Picture, then Forward, Back and Delete for the one selected.
3. Click the words on the slide and type. ⌥↩ breaks the slide at the caret; ⇧⌘N starts a new one; Esc stops typing.
4. Hover the words to see the text box. Drag a corner or side handle to resize it, or its edge to move it. Shapes and pictures move and resize the same way; the arrow keys nudge them.
5. The slides run down the left (along the bottom in the small view). Drag one to move it; its … menu duplicates, groups or deletes it; the + at the end adds one.
6. Page Up and Page Down move between slides. In Edit, the arrow keys, Space and Enter never change what the room sees.
You can edit a slide while it’s live: the screen keeps the old version until you press Update live.
Editing something that’s already in the playlist opens a smaller editor beside the playlist and output. The expand button at the top right switches between the two. Expanded, the panel on the right (Slide or Song, and Text) is always open.

import.a:
1. Choose Import in the + menu.
2. Pick a PowerPoint or PDF file.
PowerPoint comes in as editable text slides; PDF brings each page in as a picture. From Keynote, export to PowerPoint or PDF first.

web.a:
1. Choose Web page in the + menu.
2. Enter a secure (https) address.
3. Show it like any slide: it appears on the audience screens in an isolated view.
Black screen covers it.

props.q: Show a logo or notice over everything
props.a:
1. Open Show controls › Props.
2. Make a prop from a picture or a line of text.
3. Click it to show or hide it over everything.
Messages show text such as “Parent of {number}” as a lower third or a ticker.

timers.a:
1. For a full-screen countdown, add a Countdown item and show it.
2. For a timer the stage can see, start one in Show controls › Timers.
Running timers show on the stage display.

stage.a:
1. Click the Audience or Stage light in the toolbar to open Screens.
2. Give a screen the Stage role.
It shows the current and next slide, the clock, timers, chords and your stage message. To see the next slide yourself without a stage screen, click Next above the live monitor (Room brings it back).

themes.a:
1. Click Theme in the toolbar.
2. Choose the kind of slide (Scripture, Lyrics, Text) and the layout (Full screen or Lower third).
3. Click a theme and choose where to use it: all outputs, or only the main screens, the alternate HDMI output or the stream.
The strip at the top shows what each output uses; “Follow main” puts an output back with the main screens. Click Edit on a theme to change its fonts, colours, effects (such as Dim, to darken the background behind the words) and background; a built-in theme is saved as a new theme of your own, and the original stays as it is. Import theme and the export button move themes between computers.

text.q: Format the words: font, colour, capitals, lists
text.a:
1. Open the item in Edit and pick the Text tab on the right (for a quick change during the service, select the item and click Text in the toolbar instead).
2. Choose the font and size, then B, I, U and S for bold, italic, underline and strikethrough. Alignment sets left, centre or right, and top, middle or bottom.
3. The row of icons under them switches options on and off: AB for all capitals, the arrows for shrink to fit, the wrap for joining the lines into one, bullets or numbers for a list, and the clock or calendar to show the time or the date instead of the words. Hover an icon to see its name.
4. Below: Stroke and Shadow, Lines only (a bar behind each line) and Scrolling (a ticker across the screen).
5. Copy style takes this formatting to Paste style onto another song or item.
A song’s formatting stays with the song, so it looks the same in every playlist; a slide item’s stays with the item. Use theme puts everything back the way the theme has it.

logo.q: Set the logo and off-air screen
logo.a:
1. Open Settings › Presenting.
2. Type your church name and a tagline and pick a look, or choose your own picture or video.
The off-air screen shows it whenever nothing is live.

backup.q: Back up or move your library
backup.a:
1. Open Settings › Library & backups.
2. Click Export library to save everything (songs, playlists, themes, media) to one file.
3. On the other computer, click Import library and pick that file.
A backup is also made every day.

undo.a:
1. Press {{undo}} (or Edit › Undo in the menu bar) to undo a change to playlists, songs or slides.
2. Press {{redo}} to redo it.
Things that can’t be undone (deleting media from the library, removing a package, going live on a stream) ask first.

announcements.a:
1. Add Announcements from the + menu and give each notice its own slide.
2. In its header, the film strip sets how many seconds each slide shows.
3. Show it: the slides move on by themselves and loop. Choose “Off: wait for a click” to step through them by hand.
4. To run them over whatever else is on screen, click the target in the header: they play on the announcements layer (it turns green). While a full-screen announcement shows, the slide’s words underneath fade out, so the two never overlap; an announcement laid out as a lower third or along the top leaves them showing.
For a lobby screen that shows only the announcements, give it a Look that shows just the background and announcements.

audio.q: Play music or a video without it starting by itself
audio.a:
1. Click a song or sound in Media › Audio to select it; nothing plays yet.
2. Press its play button (or Play in the room) when you want it.
3. Videos can wait for Play too: set Settings › Video › When a video goes live to wait. A clicked cue or slide then holds its first frame until you press Play. The play button on a media tile always starts it at once.

fitScreens.q: Fit the picture to a projector (keystone, flips, colour)
fitScreens.a:
1. Open Settings › Screens › Fit each screen and pick the screen.
2. Switch on its test pattern, then drag each corner of the shape to where the picture should reach on the wall (or select a corner and use the arrow keys; Shift for bigger steps).
3. Size and Across / Up-down move the whole picture; Mirror left–right is for rear projection, Upside down for a ceiling mount.
4. Brightness, Contrast, Saturation and Hue match its colour to the other screens.
Only that screen changes, never the slides. Reset puts it back; the settings stay with the projector even if the displays are re-arranged.

edgeBlend.q: Blend several projectors into one wide picture
edgeBlend.a:
1. Give each projector the Audience role in Outputs.
2. In Settings › Screens › Edge blending, switch on “Blend the audience screens”.
3. Set their order left to right, and the Overlap: how much neighbouring pictures overlap on the wall.
4. If the overlaps look darker than the rest, raise the Gamma; brighter, lower it.
The words sit in the middle of the wide picture. To try it without projectors, switch on the rehearsal window: 2–4 windows stand in for them.

multiview.q: See every screen and camera at once (multi-view)
multiview.a:
1. Open Outputs (from the Audience or Stage light) › More output types › Open multi-view.
2. A window opens with Program, Preview, the next slide, the stage display, the alternate output, the stream and every camera. Move it to a spare monitor.
Red marks what's on air, green what's waiting. It only watches: nothing in it changes the screens.

lists.q: Make a bulleted or numbered list
lists.a:
1. Open the slides in Edit and type each point on its own line.
2. In the Text tab on the right, click the bullets icon or the numbers icon.
Each line becomes a point. A slide’s heading stays a heading: only the lines under it are numbered. Click the same icon again to go back to plain lines.

colours.q: Pick a colour, or save your own
colours.a:
1. Click any colour swatch (the text colour in the Text tab, a shape’s fill, a theme’s colours).
2. Pick from the palette: greys along the top, strong colours under them, then lighter and darker shades.
3. For any other colour, click + under Custom: choose it in the system picker, and it’s saved there for next time. The dropper picks a colour from anywhere on the screen.
Your custom colours are shared by every colour swatch in Lampstand and kept in your backups. Reset (where it shows) goes back to the theme’s colour.

step.q: Step through the slides from the monitor
step.a:
1. Put a slide from a song, verse or slide set on the screens.
2. Under the live monitor, click ▶ for the next slide or ◀ for the previous one.
3. At the end of an item, ▶ carries on to the first slide of the next item in the playlist, into the next section too (section headings are skipped). At the start, ◀ goes back to the last slide of the item before.
4. The slides either side show small next to the buttons (“Next item” when it’s the next item’s). Hover one to see it large enough to read; click it to put it straight on the screens.
The arrow keys ({{next}} / {{previous}}) stop at the end of an item, so a song never runs into the next by accident. The stream shows the same as the screens, so it changes with them; if it’s showing something else, Send to stream on the monitor puts the screens on it.

everything.title: Everything Lampstand does
everything.help: Every feature that works today, by area. Planned ones are listed in Settings › Features.

desk.title: Cameras, sound desks and controllers
desk.help: Switching cameras, bringing in the sound desk, and running Lampstand from a desk or controller over MIDI or OSC.

cameras.a:
1. Open Media › Sources › Video input.
2. Click a camera to put it on Preview.
3. Press Cut ({{switcherCut}}) or Auto ({{switcherAuto}}) to take it to the screen, or drag the T-bar to mix by hand. Pick the transition (Cut, Fade, Dip or Wipe) and its length beside them.
Double-click a camera to take it at once. Keys 1–9 preview a camera, Shift+1–9 take it. PiP puts a second camera in a corner. The Switcher button hides Preview and Program when you want bigger cameras. Slide words stay on top of the camera.
For one-click looks, use Scenes under the live monitor: Slides, a camera with the slide or with a lower third, or two cameras side by side or in a corner. Any camera the computer sees works: USB webcams, HDMI/SDI capture cards, or virtual cameras (OBS, NDI Webcam Input).

deskSound.q: Bring the sound desk into Lampstand
deskSound.a:
1. Connect the desk by USB (or through an audio interface). Install its driver if the maker provides one; many desks need none on a Mac.
2. On the desk, send the main mix to USB channels 1–2 (Lampstand takes the first two channels).
3. In the Live console, pick it in the mic box under the scenes (or open Media › Sources › Audio input and click Stream on it).
4. Check the L/R meter on the stream picture moves when someone speaks. The input meters read in decibels like the desk’s own: speech usually sits around the middle; if it stays near the left, raise the desk’s USB send (or the input’s level in Windows’ sound settings).
5. A desk can show many inputs (IN 1-2, IN 3-4…). In Audio inputs, click Choose and tick only the ones you use; the others leave the lists.
Leave Room off for mics and the desk: the desk already puts them on the room’s speakers, and playing them twice echoes.

midi.q: Run Lampstand from a desk or MIDI controller
midi.a:
1. Plug the desk or controller in by USB (or a MIDI interface).
2. Open Settings › Control surfaces and check it shows under MIDI.
3. Under Controls, choose what a control should do: a show action (next slide, go live, black…), a camera, a mixer fader or mute, or the T-bar.
4. Press Learn, then move the fader or press the button on the desk.
5. Try it: the control now does that.
The Activity row shows the last control Lampstand heard. Press Learn again to change a control; the bin removes it.

osc.q: Connect a desk or app over the network (OSC)
osc.a:
1. Open Settings › Control surfaces and turn on “OSC over the network”.
2. Type the address and port the page shows into the desk or app.
3. Enter the desk’s own address and OSC port under “The desk’s address” (an X32 or M32 uses 10023).
4. For a Behringer X32 or Midas M32, turn on “Ask the desk for its changes”, or its faders and mutes won’t reach Lampstand.
5. Add controls with Learn, as for MIDI.
Both computers must be on the same network. A learned X32 mute (its /mix/on switch) is set up as “on means the channel is on” by itself.

feedback.q: Keep motor faders and button lights in step
feedback.a:
1. Open Settings › Control surfaces.
2. Leave “Motor faders and button lights follow” on.
When you change a fader or a mute in Lampstand, the desk’s motorised fader moves and its button light matches. A fader you’re moving on the desk is left alone, so it never fights your hand.

cues.q: Make the desk react to the show (mute a mic while a video plays)
cues.a:
1. Open Settings › Control surfaces › Send to the desk and click Add a cue.
2. Choose when: a video starts or stops, a camera goes on or off, the stream goes live or ends, the screen goes black or is cleared.
3. Choose the message: MIDI (port, CC, note or program change, channel, number, value) or OSC (address and value).
4. Click Test to send it now and check the desk responds.
Example: to mute channel 5 on an X32 while a video plays, send OSC /ch/05/mix/on with the whole number 0 when a video starts, and 1 when it stops.

deskTrouble.a:
1. Open Settings › Control surfaces and watch the Activity row while you move the control.
2. Nothing shows, MIDI: check the cable, that the desk is listed under MIDI, and that the desk is set to send MIDI in its own setup.
3. Nothing shows, OSC: check the port, that the desk points at the address shown, that both are on the same network, and that a firewall isn’t blocking it. For an X32 or M32, turn on “Ask the desk for its changes”.
4. It shows but nothing happens: press Learn for that control again (the desk may send on another channel or number).
5. A mute works backwards: change “The desk’s control is” under that control.

media-tags.description: Label media (Christmas, youth, walk-in) and keep collections that fill themselves by tag.

media-relink.name: Replace or relink file
media-relink.description: Swap a clip for a new version everywhere it is used, or find a file that moved.

media-optimise.name: Optimise for playback
media-optimise.description: Convert heavy or unusual videos to a smooth, projector-friendly format in the background.

playlist-folders.name: Playlist folders
playlist-folders.description: Group media playlists into folders (per series, season or ministry).

media-favourites.name: Favourites
media-favourites.description: Star pictures, videos and audio and find them all in the Favourites view of the media bin.

media-playlists.name: Media playlists
media-playlists.description: Group pictures and videos into your own playlists in the media bin: drag media onto a playlist, reorder it, and import straight into it.

message-tokens.name: Live clocks in messages
message-tokens.description: Put a running timer or the time of day inside a message, e.g. "Service starts in {timer}".

custom-clear-groups.name: Custom clear groups
custom-clear-groups.description: One button that clears exactly the layers you choose, e.g. slide and props but not the background: Settings › Presenting › Clear groups, used from the “…” beside the monitor.

syphon.name: Syphon output
syphon.description: Share outputs with other apps on the same Mac, like OBS (needs the Syphon framework).

output-adjust.name: Screen adjustments
output-adjust.description: Keystone, corner pinning, scaling, flips and colour correction for each screen (Settings › Screens).

timecode.name: Timecode
timecode.description: Follow timecode from audio or video gear to fire slides on time.

playback-markers.name: Playback markers
playback-markers.description: Markers on a video that trigger actions or stage messages at set moments.

multitracks.name: MultiTracks
multitracks.description: Import lyrics, chord charts and cues from MultiTracks.

stage-app.name: Stage app
stage-app.description: Show the stage display on a phone or tablet for musicians.

connections.streaming: Stream to YouTube, Facebook or any RTMP service, and record — set it up in Streaming.

canvas.collapse: Show the playlist and output beside the editor

import.pdfStarted: Importing the PDF, one picture per page…

web.invalid: Use a full secure address, starting with https://

sidebar.noTemplates: No templates yet: save a playlist as a template in Playlists.
sidebar.confirmDelete: Delete the playlist “{{name}}”? Its songs and media stay in the library.

textBar.sizeHelp: Largest text size; long slides still shrink to fit.

mediaBin.noPlaylists: Group media into playlists: click + and drag pictures or videos onto it.
mediaBin.deleted: Deleted “{{name}}”. The media is still in your library.

mediaBin.noFavourites: No favourites yet. Hover over any media and click the star to keep it here.
mediaBin.deleteConfirm: Delete “{{name}}” from the library? Its file is removed too, and this can’t be undone.

playback.trimHelpUnknown: It starts at the in-point, and stops (or loops, or moves on) at the out-point.

clearGroups.title: Clear groups
clearGroups.help: Each group is one button in the “…” menu beside the monitor that clears exactly the layers you tick. Anything it clears can be brought back from its layer button.
clearGroups.name: Group name

masks.title: Masks
masks.help: A mask shapes an output: bring the edges in, round the corners, use an oval, or use a picture (white shows, black hides). Everything outside the shape is black. The stage display is never masked.
masks.noOutputs: No screens are connected yet; the Program monitor shows the audience mask.

roleHelp.main: Projectors and TVs the room sees. The Program monitor shows this shape too.

masks.name: Mask name
masks.imageHelp: White areas of the picture show, black areas hide. Grey fades in between.

looks.title: Looks
looks.help: A Look decides which layers each kind of screen shows, e.g. “Lobby”: secondary screens show only the background. Switch Looks from the toolbar; the change is instant.
looks.name: Look name

audio.nothingHint: click a track to listen first
audio.empty: No audio yet. Import music or sound effects with the upload button.
audio.emptyPlaylist: This playlist is empty. Add tracks from All audio with their … menu, or import into it.
audio.rowHint: Click to listen on this computer first; double-click to play it in the room
audio.previewHint: Only you hear this — the room doesn't
audio.rowHintRoom: Click to play it in the room; double-click does the same

inputs.noCameras: No cameras or capture cards found. Plug one in and it appears here.
inputs.noMics: No microphones or audio inputs found.
inputs.camerasFootnote: Saved for each camera on this computer. While a camera is on screen, changes show straight away. The same settings are in each camera’s … menu in Media › Video input.
inputs.allHidden: Every camera is switched off for Media. Turn one on in Settings › Video.

access.title: Lampstand can’t use the cameras yet
access.ask: Your computer asks once before an app can use its cameras and capture cards.
access.refused: Camera access was turned off for Lampstand. Turn it on in your computer’s privacy settings, then look again.

inputs.lookAgainHelp: Look again for cameras and capture cards (after plugging one in)
inputs.hintPreview: Click a camera to put it on Preview, then Cut or Auto. Double-click takes it straight to the screen; keys 1–9 preview, Shift+1–9 take.
inputs.hintProgram: Click a camera to put it on the screen; click it again to take it off.
inputs.switcherHelp: Show or hide Preview, Program, Cut and Auto (hide it to see your cameras bigger)
inputs.switchHelp: While a camera is on screen, the same switch sits under the Live monitor, and in Media › Video input.

micAccess.title: Lampstand can’t use the microphones yet
micAccess.ask: Your computer asks once before an app can use its microphones and audio inputs.
micAccess.refused: Microphone access was turned off for Lampstand. Turn it on in your computer’s privacy settings, then look again.

inputs.overCameraHelp: Replace the camera with the slide and its background, or keep the camera under the words (for lyrics over a camera shot).
inputs.toRoomHelp: Out of this computer's room speakers. Usually off: the desk already puts mics in the room, and playing them twice echoes.
inputs.toStreamHelp: Heard on the livestream and in the recording.
inputs.noneChosen: No inputs chosen: pick the ones you use with Choose.

stock.hint: Drawn by Lampstand itself: works offline, free to use, sharp on any screen. Click one to show it now; its … menu puts it behind the selected item’s slides.
stock.addCountdown_one: Add a {{count}}-minute countdown to the playlist
stock.addCountdown_other: Add a {{count}}-minute countdown to the playlist
stock.countdownAdded_one: Added a {{count}}-minute countdown to the playlist.
stock.countdownAdded_other: Added a {{count}}-minute countdown to the playlist.

itemBg.title: Behind these slides
itemBg.own: These slides have their own background (click to change)
itemBg.theme: These slides use their theme’s background (click to choose another)
itemBg.noneYet: None yet: add some in Media › Backgrounds
itemBg.pickItemFirst: Select an item to use it behind its slides
itemBg.useForAll_one: Use behind every item in the service ({{count}})
itemBg.useForAll_other: Use behind every item in the service ({{count}})
itemBg.copyToAllHint: Every song, reading, presentation, announcement and countdown in the service gets this background (or the theme’s, if this one uses the theme’s)
itemBg.change: Change the background of these slides
itemBg.soundOn: The background video’s sound is on (click to mute it)
itemBg.soundOff: The background video is silent (click to hear it)
itemBg.soundHint: Heard in the room (Settings › Audio › room output) and on the stream, like any video

audioSettings.roomHelp: Tracks from the Audio tab, live audio inputs and the sound of videos play here, from the main output (or this computer when there’s no output).
audioSettings.roomOutputHelp: The speakers or mixer the room hears.
audioSettings.fadeHelp: How long Fade out in the Audio tab takes to reach silence.
audioSettings.listenHelp: Where you hear a track when you click it in the Audio tab, before the room does (headphones, say).
audioSettings.inputsHelp: Speak or play into an input to see its level. Put one through the room from the Audio tab.
audioSettings.clickHelp: In the Audio tab. Double-click always plays it in the room.
audioSettings.startVolumeHelp: Off: each track keeps the volume the last one had.
audioSettings.fixedVolume: Start every track at a set volume
audioSettings.afterTrack: At the end of a track
audioSettings.afterTrackHelp: For tracks played from a playlist.
audioSettings.loopHelp: After the last track, start again from the top.
audioSettings.mixerHelp: Every source has a channel: level, mute, solo to your headphones, EQ, compressor, and whether the room and the stream hear it.
audioSettings.openMixerHelp: {{count}} channels. The mixer docks along the bottom of the window.

main.title: Audience screens
main.tip: Audience screens: choose where the room sees the show

stage.title: Stage screens
stage.tip: Stage screens: choose where the speaker sees what’s next

screensMenu.windowHint: Show it in a window on this screen

stageLayouts.name: Layout name
stageLayouts.presetHelp: A ready-made layout. Duplicate it to move things around, resize them, or add your own text.
stageLayouts.editHelp: Drag a box to move it, its corner to resize it. Arrow keys nudge the selected box (Shift: further); Delete removes it.
stageLayouts.selectHint: Select a box on the layout to change it.

live.noFfmpeg: Lampstand needs its video encoder (ffmpeg) to stream and record, and couldn’t find it on this computer.
live.confirmStart: Start the livestream to {{names}}? Everyone watching will see what the stream shows.
live.noDestinations: Add where to stream (YouTube, Facebook…) in Stream settings first.

errors.noDestinations: No destination could start: check each one has its stream key.
errors.destinationFailed: A destination stopped (check its key and the internet connection).
errors.encoderStopped: The encoder stopped and couldn’t restart.
errors.recordingFolderFailed: Couldn’t record: the recording folder can’t be used. Choose another in Settings › Streaming.
errors.reconnectFailed: The stream couldn’t reconnect for 10 minutes and stopped. Check the internet connection, then Go live again.

live.coverHelp: Hide what’s happening from the stream: viewers see the cover picture (Settings › Streaming) until you show the stream again. The sound carries on.
live.uncoverHelp: The stream shows the cover picture. Click to show the service again.

streaming.destinationsHelp: Stream keys are stored encrypted on this computer and never shown again.
streaming.noDestinations: No destinations yet. Add one above.

help.udp: The other computer's IP address and a free port. There, in OBS: Media Source, untick “Local file”, Input udp://@:{{port}}. In VLC: Open Network, udp://@:{{port}}.
help.srt: The receiver's address and port. It listens there: in OBS, Media Source, untick “Local file”, Input srt://:{{port}}?mode=listener. Lost packets are resent, so it suits a link between sites.

direct.noSrt: The ffmpeg on this computer was built without SRT, so this link can't start yet. UDP works now.

ways.title: Ways to go live
ways.help: Use one or several at once: they all carry the same picture and sound.

service.title: A streaming service
service.body: YouTube, Facebook or any service with an RTMP address, for people watching online. Paste the stream key the service gives you. The delay is set by the service (on YouTube: Stream latency › Ultra low-latency).

direct.title: A direct link
direct.body: Straight to a computer you run (OBS, vMix, VLC or a decoder box): an overflow room, another campus, a second streaming computer. No key: you type the receiver's address.

ndi.title: NDI
ndi.body: To vMix, OBS and other NDI gear on this network, as the program, the words alone to key over cameras, or the stream picture. It sends whenever a feed is on; no Go live needed.
ndi.needsTools: Needs the free NDI Tools installed on this computer.

streaming.keyStored: Key saved. Paste a new one to replace it.

keyHelp.youtube: YouTube Studio › Go live › Stream: copy the “Stream key”.
keyHelp.facebook: Facebook › Live video › Streaming software: copy the “Stream key”.
keyHelp.custom: From your streaming service. Some services put the key in the address instead.

streaming.pictureHelp: The stream can show something different from the projector: e.g. the camera with the lyrics as a lower third.
streaming.wordsAlignHelp: Where the lower third sits across the picture. Picking a theme starts it where the theme was designed to sit.
streaming.wordsThemeHelp: Draw the stream's lower third with a theme made for it, whatever the projector shows. Make your own in Themes with the Lower third layout.
streaming.wordsSizeHelp: How big the lower-third words are, as a share of their full-screen size.
streaming.wordsAutoOn: Fits each slide to the band.
streaming.wordsAutoHelp: Long verses shrink to fit the lower third; short lines stay large. Turn off to choose one size.
streaming.wordsHelp: Lower third: smaller, along the bottom, over a soft band.
streaming.backgroundHelp: What the projector shows, a camera, the video switcher’s program, two cameras together, or black.
streaming.cameraHelp: Used when “Behind the words” is Camera.
streaming.qualityHelp: 720p at 30 fps suits most church internet connections.
streaming.qualityLive: Changes apply the next time you go live or record.
streaming.bitrateHelp: Recommended: {{kbps}} kb/s. Your upload speed should be at least 1.5× this.
streaming.encoderHelp: In use: {{encoder}}. Automatic keeps the picture on the graphics card and uses its hardware encoder (smoothest, least effort). A specific encoder uses the standard path instead.
streaming.recordWhileHelp: Keep a copy of every livestream on this computer.
streaming.soundMixerHelp: What the stream hears comes from the mixer: switch each channel on or off here, or set levels and EQ on the mixer.
streaming.delayHelp: Hold the stream's sound back so it lines up with a camera that runs late.
streaming.performanceHelp: How hard streaming works this computer. Older or busy computers stream smoothly in Light.

modeHelp.auto: Picks Light, Balanced or Quality for this computer (from “Check this computer” when it has been run).
modeHelp.light: 960×540 at 30 fps, 2 Mb/s, the lightest encoder settings and a slower preview. For older laptops and slow internet.
modeHelp.balanced: 1280×720 at 30 fps, 3.5 Mb/s. Good for most churches.
modeHelp.quality: 1920×1080 at 30 fps, 6 Mb/s. Needs a recent computer (ideally with a hardware encoder) and a good upload.
modeHelp.custom: The size, frame rate and bitrate below, exactly as set.

streaming.wordsWidthHelp: How far across the picture the words may spread. Wider: fewer, longer lines.
streaming.coverHelp: What the stream shows while it’s covered (the Cover button in the Live console): the logo card, or one of your pictures or videos.

surfaces.midiNone: No MIDI devices found. Plug the desk or controller in by USB (or a MIDI interface); it shows here straight away.
surfaces.midiUnavailable: MIDI isn't available on this computer.
surfaces.oscHelp: For desks and apps that speak OSC (Behringer X32 and Midas M32, TouchOSC, many digital desks). Lampstand listens on this port.
surfaces.oscFailed: Lampstand couldn't listen on port {{port}}: another app may be using it. Try another port.
surfaces.oscSendHere: Point the desk or app at {{addresses}}, port {{port}}.
surfaces.deskAddressHelp: Where OSC cues and fader positions go (the desk's IP address and its OSC port; an X32 listens on 10023).
surfaces.feedback: Motor faders and button lights follow
surfaces.feedbackHelp: Send fader positions and mutes back, so motorised faders move and button lights match when you change the mixer in Lampstand.
surfaces.activityHelp: The last control Lampstand heard: move one to check it's connected.
surfaces.controlsHelp: Choose what a control does, press Learn, then move the fader or press the button on the desk.
surfaces.noControls: No controls yet. Choose what one should do below, press Learn and touch it on the desk.
surfaces.touchIt: Move a fader or press a button…
surfaces.cuesHelp: When something happens in Lampstand, tell the desk: mute the pulpit mic while a video plays, recall a scene when the stream starts.
surfaces.sendAs: Send as MIDI or OSC when: {{name}}
surfaces.oscNoAddress: Set the desk's address above, or this cue goes nowhere.
surfaces.subscribe: Ask the desk for its changes (X32, M32)
surfaces.subscribeHelp: Behringer X32 and Midas M32 desks only send their fader and mute moves to apps that keep asking. Turn this on (with the desk's address above) and Lampstand asks every 8 seconds.
surfaces.muteModeOf: How the mute control for {{name}} reports

muteModes.toggle: A button: each press mutes or unmutes
muteModes.on: A switch: on means the channel is on (X32, M32)

mixer.title: Mixer
mixer.processing: High-pass, EQ and compressor (click to edit)
mixer.soloHelp: Solo plays a channel on your “Listen on” output (headphones). The room and the stream don't change.
mixer.limiterHelp: Keeps the mix under −1 dBFS so a shout never clips.
mixer.name: Channel name
mixer.delayOf: Stream sound delay (line up with a late camera)
mixer.noMoreInputs: Every input is on the mixer already.
mixer.addHint: Add a microphone or the sound desk's feed with “Add input”.
mixer.resetConfirm: Put every level, EQ and compressor back to flat? Inputs and routing are kept.

switcher.title: Switcher
switcher.tbarHelp: Drag down to mix the Preview camera in by hand. Let go past half-way to finish the take.
switcher.clickHelp: Preview first: a click puts it on Preview, then Cut (⇧C) or Auto (⇧T) takes it to the screen; double-click takes it at once. Keys 1–9 preview a camera, Shift+1–9 take it.
switcher.pipHelp: Where the second camera's box sits (choose the camera in the switcher).

ndi.feedsHelp: Each feed is a source other NDI software sees on the network.
ndi.noFeeds: No feeds yet. Add one for the program, or one for the words alone to key over your cameras.
ndi.name: Feed name (seen on the network)

contentHelp.program: Everything the main screen shows: backgrounds, videos, cameras and words.
contentHelp.words: Only the slide's words, with a transparent background (alpha), to key over cameras in vMix, OBS or a hardware switcher.
contentHelp.stream: The same picture as the livestream (Settings › Streaming › What it shows).

ndi.noRuntime: NDI needs the free NDI runtime, which comes with NDI Tools. Install it, then restart Lampstand.
ndi.loadFailed: The NDI runtime is installed but didn't start: {{message}}
ndi.howReceiveHelp: In vMix, OBS (with the NDI plugin) or NDI Studio Monitor, add an NDI source and pick this computer's feed by its name.
ndi.howKeyHelp: Add a “Words (alpha)” feed and put it on top of your camera in the receiving software: the background is see-through.
ndi.trademark: NDI® is a registered trademark of Vizrt NDI AB. Lampstand uses the NDI runtime installed on this computer and doesn't include it.

console.title: Live
console.popOut: Open the Live console in its own window
console.showBefore: Show the stream picture before going live
console.previewOff: Turn on “Show the stream picture before going live” to check what the stream will show.
console.previewLight: The picture shows here once you go live or record (Light mode saves the computer's effort before then).
console.healthIdle: Frame rate, bitrate, encoder speed and the computer's load show here while you stream or record.
console.advice: This computer is struggling to keep up. Light mode streams smoothly with a smaller picture (a two-second pause, and the recording carries on).
console.adviceUpload: Your internet upload is only carrying about {{rate}} Mb/s, too little for this picture size. Light mode (540p) will look sharper and smoother (a two-second pause, and the recording carries on).
console.noDestinations: Nowhere to stream yet. Use Add to choose a service such as YouTube, or a direct link to another room.

kindHelp.youtube: Paste the stream key from YouTube Studio.
kindHelp.facebook: Paste the stream key from Facebook Live.
kindHelp.custom: Any service that gives an RTMP address and key.
kindHelp.direct: Straight to OBS, vMix or VLC in another room. Under a second of delay.
kindHelp.ndi: To vMix, OBS and NDI gear on this network. Set up in Settings.

console.quickLocked: Stop the stream or recording to change the mode.

help.fps: Frames per second going out (target {{target}}). Green: smooth.
help.speed: Encoder speed: 1.00× keeps up with real time; below 0.95× the computer is falling behind.
help.delay: Sending delay: how far behind live the stream is when it leaves this computer. Viewers see this plus the service's own delay (on YouTube, set Stream latency to “Ultra low-latency” in YouTube Studio for the shortest).
help.load: Computer load: Lampstand and the encoder together (100% = one full core).
help.size: Picture size and frame rate for the next start ({{mode}} mode).
help.bitrate: Video bitrate (target {{target}} Mb/s): how much internet upload the stream uses.
help.encoder: The video encoder in use (a hardware one saves the computer's effort).
help.bitrateAdapted: The upload couldn't carry {{target}} Mb/s, so the stream lowered itself to {{rate}} Mb/s to stay live. It climbs back when the connection allows.

console.streamMuted: The stream is muted: viewers hear nothing

silent.muted: The stream is muted: viewers hear nothing.
silent.nothing: Viewers hear nothing: no channel goes to the stream. Switch on the mics or desk below (Sound).
silent.quiet: Viewers hear nothing: {{names}} go to the stream, but there's no sound on them. Check the mic or desk is on and its level is up.
silent.low: Viewers hear nothing: the levels are turned right down ({{levels}}), so even speech is too quiet to reach them. Turn them up, or use the sliders below.

console.soundHelp: Switched on: the stream hears it.
console.micOnStream: On the stream: click to take it off
console.micOffStream: Off the stream: click to send it
console.lowerThirdOn: The words run along the bottom of the stream picture.
console.lowerThirdHelp: Show the words along the bottom, over a camera or the slides.
console.lowerThirdMirror: The stream shows a screen now, as it is.
console.fadeHelp: When the stream changes scene or camera: a cut, or a fade this long.

benchmark.help: A 10-second test that finds the streaming mode this computer handles smoothly. Auto uses the answer.
benchmark.done: This computer streams smoothly in {{mode}} (encoder: {{encoder}}). Auto will use it.

transition.itemDefault: Transition: the default (click to give these slides their own)

advance.title: Move on by itself
advance.loop: Loop back to the first slide
advance.help: The slides move on by themselves every {{s}} s while live (click to change)
advance.offHelp: The slides wait for a click (click to make them move on by themselves)

screenFit.title: Fit each screen
screenFit.help: Pin each projector's picture to where it really lands (keystone), size and move it, flip it for rear projection, and match its colour to the other screens. Only that screen changes.
screenFit.noScreens: No screen to fit yet: give a display a role in Outputs, or switch on the rehearsal window.
screenFit.cornerHint: Drag, or use the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps)
screenFit.cornerHelp: Drag each corner to where the picture should reach on the wall. Switch on the test pattern to line it up.
screenFit.flipHHelp: For rear projection: the projector shines from behind the screen.
screenFit.flipVHelp: For a projector mounted upside down on the ceiling.

edgeBlend.title: Edge blending
edgeBlend.help: Several projectors side by side make one wide picture. They overlap a little and the overlaps fade, so no seam shows.
edgeBlend.enableHelp: Every screen set to Audience shows its part of one wide picture.
edgeBlend.needTwo: Give two or more displays the Audience role in Outputs to blend them.
edgeBlend.gammaHelp: Raise the gamma if the overlaps look darker than the rest, lower it if they look brighter. 2.2 suits most projectors.
edgeBlend.windowsHelp: How many windows stand in for the projectors while you rehearse.
edgeBlend.orderHelp: The order the projectors stand in, as seen by the room.

overlay.title: Readability overlay
overlay.help: Darken the background so the words stand out

color.fromScreen: Pick a colour from the screen
